name: Judith
description: Daughter of Merari, of the tribe of Simeon; widow of Manasses for three years and four months, fasting and wearing sackcloth in her widowhood; hearing that Ozias had sworn to surrender Bethulia to the Assyrians after five days, she rebuked the people's oath, adorned herself, went out with her maid to the Assyrian camp, was brought before Holofernes, stayed three days in his camp, and on the fourth night, while he lay drunk with wine, took his fauchion and cut off his head; she carried the head back to Bethulia, was blessed by Ozias and all Israel, led Israel in a song of thanksgiving, dedicated Holofernes' goods to the Lord, returned to Bethulia, lived to be a hundred and five years old, freed her maid before she died, and was buried beside her husband Manasses

points: Sisters, this is for you too; there is no sitting on your hands saying, I am just going to have babies, I have nothing to do. Judith fell upon her face, put ashes upon her head, and cried with a loud voice. Sisters, you have to cry with a loud voice: while we are out there prophesying and going in the scriptures, you need to be praying for the prophets, praying for the children to get their minds right, praying for our nation to rise up.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

source.name: TIPNR, Translators Individualised Proper Names with all References, by Tyndale House Cambridge, STEPBible.org
